approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2018

The Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2018 was supported on schedules 1 and 4, and an amendment was moved noting the Coalition Government's failure to improve tax haven transparency.

The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2018 strengthens tax integrity by closing loopholes for multinational tax avoidance, including through the Multinational Anti-Avoidance Law (MAAL), and tightening eligibility for small business capital gains tax (CGT) concessions. The bill also clarifies tax rules to allow venture capital investments in fin-tech businesses, with the ATO estimating over $7 billion in annual sales revenue added to the tax base and 38 multinationals, including Google and Facebook, changing their tax affairs.

The speaker argued that the Turnbull government has failed to act on tax havens and multinational tax avoidance, leaving loopholes open despite public demand for action. Labor proposed a tax haven transparency package including public country-by-country reporting, whistleblower protections, and tax domicile disclosure for government tenders, while criticising the government for prioritising $80 billion in big business tax cuts over closing loopholes that cost billions in lost revenue.

The bill amends tax laws to prevent multinational tax avoidance, target small business capital gains tax concessions to genuine small businesses from 1 July 2017, clarify venture capital rules for fintech investment, and exempt Defence Force Ombudsman reparation payments from income tax.
